In our project we purified 225 uL of homogenate using the KingFisher‱ Cell and Tissue DNA Kit - THERMO SCIENTIFIC‱ (discontinued) on a KingFisher Flex robot - THERMO SCIENTIFIC‱ (ref. 5400620).

steps.title: Prepare Working Stations
steps.instruction: Divide the lab bench into 30 cm wide working stations, numbering them from 1 to n+1 (where n is the total number of samples, and n+1 is for the blank sample).

substeps.instruction: Wipe all lab benches using a paper towel and 10% bleach solution.

At each station, place: 1 tray, 1 bottle for temporary homogenate storage (only for samples with ≥10 g biomass), small and large tweezers, a large petri dish, a microscope, a 200 mm silicon spatula, a 200 mm silicon corner spatula, 1 large glass petri dish, an IKA DT-50 rotor stator tube (50 mL), and 1 screw cap microtube (2.0 mL).
For the blank sample station (n+1), provide a 500 mL Nalgene HDPE bottle.
Place one drained insect bottle at each station and one empty 500 mL Nalgene HDPE wide mouth bottle at the blank station.

steps.title: Label and Clean Samples
steps.instruction: Label each bulk insect bottle and rotor stator tube with the corresponding working station number using a marker pen.

substeps.instruction: Remove any nylon circle mesh or archive labels from the bulk insect bottles using large tweezers and place them in a large glass petri dish.
Under a microscope, use small tweezers to transfer any insects stuck to the mesh or labels back into their respective bulk insect bottles.

steps.title: Add Lysis Buffer and Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add lysis buffer and Proteinase K to each insect bottle according to the biomass specifications in Table 1.

substeps.instruction: Use a graduated cylinder and a small funnel to pour lysis buffer slowly to reduce foaming.
Rinse the insect bottle walls with the buffer to ensure all specimens are soaked at the bottom.
Add Proteinase K according to Table 1 (or pre-mix Proteinase K into the total calculated lysis buffer volume before adding to bottles).

Table 1 Volumes: 
- <2g: 30mL buffer / 30μL Prot K
- 5.00–9.99g: 50mL buffer / 50μL Prot K
- 10.00–19.99g: 100mL buffer / 100μL Prot K
- 20.00–29.99g: 200mL buffer / 200μL Prot K
- 30.00–39.99g: 300mL buffer / 300μL Prot K
- >40.00g: 400mL buffer / 400μL Prot K
- Blank: 50mL buffer / 50μL Prot K

steps.title: Homogenize Samples
steps.instruction: Homogenize the insect and lysis buffer solution using an Ultra Turrax Drive with a 50 mL rotor stator tube at 6000 rpm for 2 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Pour the bulk sample into the DT-50 rotor stator tube, using spatulas to scoop out any remaining insects, and close with the lid.
For samples ≥ 100 mL, process in 50 mL batches, transferring each batch into a storage bottle until the entire sample is processed.
For the blank, homogenize 50 mL of lysis buffer solution.
Spray the UltraTurrax instrument with 10% bleach after each sample.

Allow the sample to sit until foam subsides, then transfer the homogenate back to the original insect bottle (or the 500 mL HDPE bottle for the blank), using a spatula to recover all material from the tube walls.

steps.title: Incubate Samples
steps.instruction: Perform a two-stage incubation to ensure complete lysis.

substeps.instruction: Pre-heat bottles in a 60°C water bath: 30 minutes for small samples (30, 50, 100 mL) and 40 minutes for large samples (200, 300, 400 mL).
Incubate at 56°C for 2 hours and 45 minutes in a dry shaking incubator at 90 rpm.
Return bottles to their respective working stations after incubation.

steps.title: Combine with FAVIS Lysate
steps.instruction: If the sample was previously processed via the FAVIS protocol, combine the current homogenate with the FAVIS lysate.

substeps.instruction: Thoroughly thaw the corresponding FAVIS lysate.
Pour the lysate into the homogenate bottle. Use a 1000 mL bottle for samples with 300 or 400 mL lysate.
Invert the bottle several times to mix until a clear mixture is obtained.

steps.title: Prepare Aliquots for Purification
steps.instruction: Create working-stock aliquots of the homogenate for DNA purification.

substeps.instruction: Gather a 1000 μL micropipette, 1000 μL filtered tips, and a 96-well microtube rack.
Gently shake the insect soup bottle to homogenize.
Transfer 2x900 μL aliquots (total 1.8 mL) from each bottle into corresponding 2 mL microtubes.
Fill the 96-well rack from A1 to A12, B1 to B12, etc., leaving H9 (neg control), H10 (pos control), H11 (neg lib control), and H12 (pos lib control) empty.
Label the rack with a unique ID.

steps.title: Storage
steps.instruction: Store the remaining homogenate bottles and the microtube racks at -20°C for long-term storage if not used immediately.
